nodes.description: Heterozygous loss-of-function variants in DLL1 (nonsense, splice-site, missense in the DSL domain, and whole-gene deletion) reduce the functional dosage of the Delta-like 1 Notch ligand. Premature stop codons are predicted to trigger nonsense-mediated decay, and DLL1 is strongly constrained against loss of function (gnomAD pLI = 1.0), indicating that one functional copy is insufficient.

nodes.description: Lower DLL1 ligand dosage reduces trans-activation of Notch receptors on neighboring cells. Cell-cell contact-mediated Notch receptor-ligand interaction normally releases the Notch intracellular domain, which enters the nucleus and drives target-gene transcription; reduced ligand attenuates this signaling and disrupts the lateral-inhibition and oscillatory output that patterns neural tissue.

The reduced amount of functional Delta-like 1 lowers the availability of this transmembrane ligand in the tissues where DLL1 drives Notch signaling: the neural progenitor compartment of the developing brain, and the presomitic mesoderm during somite segmentation. DLL1 is highly expressed in neuronal precursor cells during embryogenesis, and Notch output is highly sensitive to relative ligand dosage. This dosage reduction therefore feeds both a neural and a paraxial-mesoderm branch of the pathology.
